# Can wasps discriminate 'simple' artificial dorsal patterns?

Evidence that wasps can use overhead patterns comes from two
observations. First, That the proportion of choices for the rewarding
pattern ($P_{\mathrm{corr}}$) is \>50% and second, that this proportion
drops when the patterns are removed from the roof (during the control).

```{r q1Vars}
#| include: false
#| 
emmPtsArt    <- emmPtsRef %>% filter(nat_or_art == "artificial")

```

Across all artificial stimulus pairs tested, trial number had a positive effect on
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ (@fig-q2, positive slopes of solid lines) though the slope was only significant for the perpendicular-parallel and thin oblique striped stimulus pairs (@tbl-s-model-coefs). Across artificial stimulus pairs, $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ rose from between `r min(emmPtsArt$first_prob)`--`r max(emmPtsArt$first_prob)`% at trial 1 of the test phase to between `r min(emmPtsArt$last_test_prob)`--`r max(emmPtsArt$last_test_prob)`% by the end of the test phase (@fig-q2; @tbl-s-overview). For all artificial stimulus pairs, the the end-of-test $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ was significantly above chance (lower
95% CI bound \>50%; @fig-q2 test panels).

Aditionally, for the two artificial experiments that had both a test and a control phase (perpendicular-parallel and thin oblique), Wald z-tests revealed significantly higher $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the end of the test versus the start of the control phase (error bars between left and right panels in @fig-q2 are non-overlapping and the log-odds ratios between the end of test and start of control are significantly larger than zero, @tbl-s-overview). Also note that while $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is significantly above chance (grey
shaded 95% confidence ribbons in @fig-q2 do not overlap the 50% line)
from an early stage during the test phases and remain that way until the end of the
test, the $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ during the control phases is never
significantly above chance (95%
confidence ribbon always overlaps the 50% line), as one would expect for wasps
making choices in the absence of any information regarding the location
of the reward.

For the thick oblique stimulus-pair, the model suggests naive wasps perform significantly above
chance immediately (at trial 1). This is possibly due
to the model being unable to fit the rapid learning of the wasps, rather
than to the wasps having learned olfactory / temporal cues during the
pre-test training phase that persisted into the test. This is supported
by the observation that, for most artificial stimulus pairs, the proportion of correct decisions in the first few 3-trial wide
windows of the test phase (grey points in @fig-q2) are clustered around 50%.

# What information are wasps using to discriminate patterns?

```{r fig-q2}
#| fig-cap: 'Wasp reward navigation performance for artificial stimulus experiments. Each row shows one experiment; columns show test and control phases. During the test phase overhead artificial stimuli could be used by the wasps to choose the rewarding chamber; during the control phase stimuli were removed (not all experiments had a control phase). The y-axis represents the probability of a wasp to enter into the rewarding ("correct") chamber. The solid black line shows the predicted probability of correct choices across trials and the grey ribbon the 95% confidence interval around these probabilities given by our models. Grey points are the proportion of correct choices made by all wasps in 3-trial wide rolling windows. Black points represent the predicted probabilities of correct choices at the end of the test and the start of the control phases, and the error bars the 95% confidence intervals around these predictions. The dashed horizontal line represents chance performance (50%). Only the first choice of each wasp in each trial was used as data in the model and to calculate the rolling means.'
#| fig-height: 6

q2ExpOrder <- c("perpPara_170725", "thickOb_140823", "thinOb_150823", "brightDiff_250725")

emmPtsRefPlotAll <- emmAll %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder])),
    manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
  )

p <- ggplot(emmPtsRefPlotAll, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "% of decisions for reward") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 2) +
  plotStyle$themeTextEnlarged +
  facet_grid(experiment ~ manipulation, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(experiment = as_labeller(artImgLabels))) +
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(1, "lines"),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.right = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0)
)

df_rolling <- choices_rolling %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder])),
    manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
  )

p <- p + geom_point(data = df_rolling, aes(x = rank_trial, y = pcorr),

emmPtsQ2 <- emmPts %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder,

  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),

p <- p +

p <- p +
```


To answer whether wasps require optic flow contrast to discriminate
patterns we tested whether they could distinguish artificial
pattern-pairs consisting of oblique stripes oriented at either 45
degrees to the right or to the left of the y-maze arm's long axis and
the general direction of wasp travel. If wasps display a
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ \>50% and a larger $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the end of
the test relative to the start of the control, this provides evidence that wasps can
distinguish stimuli that generate identical rates of optic flow.

As already alluded to above, wasps had no trouble distinguishing between oblique stripes that
presumably produce identical rates of optic flow in the dorsal visual
field (thick and thin oblique stripe stimulus pairs in @fig-q2). 
in both the thin and thick oblique experiments $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ was 
significantly above chance (50%) by test end and for the thin oblique experiment $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at test end was
also significantly above performance at the start of the control phase (@fig-q2; @tbl-s-overview).

Next, we asked whether wasps could discriminate between an opaque and
transparent roof, ie. between stimuli that carried little to no pattern
information. As we mentioned above, performance for the thick oblique stimulus pair was significantly above chance by. 

While performance at the end of the experiment is only borderline
significantly higher than 50%, this is likely an artifact of the
increased uncertainty in the slope / effect of trial number on
performance due to the lower number of trials run in this experiment. If
one looks at the middle trials for example (@tbl-s-overview), the lower bound of
performance is considerably higher than chance.

# Can wasps use naturalistic patterns for navigation?

Evidence for whether wasps can discriminate naturalistic canopies at
above-chance rates (\>50%) is mixed. In four of the six naturalistic
canopy pairs we tested, the predicted $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ by the end of
the test was significantly / borderline significantly above chance (the lower limit of the
95% CI is \>50%; @fig-q3-tc, @tbl-s-overview), suggesting wasps may be able to
separate certain pairs of naturalistic canopies, although the
performance is generally lower than for artificial stimuli (see question 4).

```{r fig-q3-tc}
#| fig-cap: 'Wasp reward navigation performance for six naturalistic stimulus experiments. Each row shows wasp performance over two phases (columns, test and control) of an experiment. In the test phase a pair of naturalistic stimuli (at right) were shown to wasps in a Y-maze, with one of the stimuli in the pair associated with a reward and the other with no reward (see methods for further details). During the control phase the stimuli were removed but the reward remained in place. Not all experiments had a control phase (blank panels). The y-axis represents the proportion of all entries ("choices") that were into the rewarding ("correct") chamber of the maze, and so provide a measure of the wasps navigation performance in the maze. The solid black line represents the predicted mean proportion of correct decisions across trial number and the grey ribbon the 95% confidence interval around these predictions provided by the model. Grey points represent the rolling mean of the proportion of correct choices in 3-trial wide windows across all wasps present in those trials. Black points represent the predicted proportion of correct choices at the end of the test and the start of the control phases, and the error bars the 95% confidence intervals around these predictions. Only the first choice of each wasp in each trial was used as data in the model and to calculate the rolling means. The dashed horizontal line represents chance performance (50%). Note that performance is only significantly above chance for some stimulus pairs / experiments, and that predicted performance at the end of the test is rarely significantly higher than at the start of the control.'
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-pos: "p"

         trial_pos %in% c("last_test", "ctrl_start")) %>%

tbNatTcPts  <- emmPtsRef %>% filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic",
```

```{r q3Table}
q3NatPtsTable <- emmPtsTbl %>%
```

Of the four naturalistic canopies that show $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ \> 50%,
after three of those we also ran a control (patterns removed) directly
after the test phase concluded, but in only one case (Canopy E) was the
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the end of the test significantly higher than at
the start of the control. This can be attributed to the fact that
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ for the naturalistic canopies is generally not much
greater than 50% (if at all), and the fact that control experiments were
not run for many trials, increasing the uncertainty around the
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the start of the control phase.

```{r fig-q3-natart}
#| fig-cap: "End-of-test predicted performance by canopy type."

q3NatArtEndPts <- emmPts %>%
  filter(trial_pos == "last_test") %>%
  mutate(
    nat_or_art = factor(nat_or_art, levels = c("naturalistic", "artificial"))
  )

natArtMean <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  group_by(nat_or_art) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prob = mean(prob),
    min_prob  = min(prob),
    max_prob  = max(prob),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = nat_or_art,
    values_from = c(mean_prob, min_prob, max_prob),
    names_glue  = "{nat_or_art}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  mutate(diff_mean_prob = artificial_mean_prob - naturalistic_mean_prob) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_prob"), ~as.character(as.integer(round(. * 100)))))

q3NatBest  <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic") %>%
  slice_max(order_by = prob, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(prob  = as.character(as.integer(round(prob * 100))),
         label = unname(natcanLabels[experiment]))

q3ArtWorst <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "artificial") %>%
  slice_min(order_by = prob, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(prob  = as.character(as.integer(round(prob * 100))),
         label = unname(artLabels[experiment]))

ptJitter   <- position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 3)
canopyCols <- c(naturalistic = "forestgreen", artificial = "black")

```

# Performance differences among naturalistic and artificial stimuli

Discrimination performance for naturalistic canopies tends to be lower
than for artificial canopies. The naturalistic canopy showing the best
performance (`r q3NatBest$label`, $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ =
`r q3NatBest$prob`%) still has a lower $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ than the
artificial canopy with the worst performance (`r q3ArtWorst$label`,
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ = `r q3ArtWorst$prob`%). The average performance for
all naturalistic canopies is `r natArtMean$naturalistic_mean_prob`%,
whereas for artificial it is `r natArtMean$artificial_mean_prob`%, and
the difference in the average $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ for naturalistic and
artificial is `r natArtMean$diff_mean_prob`%. Given the low number of
artificial and naturalistic experiments included here (n = 4 and 7
respectively) we did not test for an overall difference between
naturalistic and artificial canopies.

```{r fig-q3-combined}
#| fig-cap: "Predicted P(correct) for naturalistic and artificial experiments at the maximum common test-phase trial across experiments. A shows predicted probability of a correct choice across all experiments in the same plot (best fit lines) and 95% confidence intervals around those probailities (shaded ribbons). The points in A show the predicted probability of a correct choice at trial 26, the maximum test-phase trial that is common to all experiments. B contrasts the performance at trial 26 between artificial and naturalistic experiments. Points in B are the same as those in A."

library(patchwork)

# Per-experiment colour mapping: black for artificial, green for naturalistic
allExpLabels <- c(artLabels, natcanLabels)
expCols <- c(
  setNames(rep("black",       length(artLabels)),    unname(artLabels)),
  setNames(rep("forestgreen", length(natcanLabels)), unname(natcanLabels))
)

# Test-phase prediction curves for all experiments
allExpTestAll <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test") %>%
  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(experiment, !!!allExpLabels))

# Maximum shared trial: highest trial number reached by every experiment
maxSharedTrial <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test") %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(max_trial = max(rank_trial), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(max_trial) %>%
  min()

# Predicted point at the shared trial for each experiment
emmSharedPt <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test", rank_trial == maxSharedTrial) %>%
  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(experiment, !!!allExpLabels))

# Panel A: overlaid learning curves
pA <- ggplot(allExpTestAll,
             aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob,
                 group = experiment, colour = experiment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL, fill = experiment),
              colour = NA, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = emmSharedPt, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = expCols, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = expCols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0.25, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial number", y = "P(correct)") +
  theme_bw()

# Panel B: jittered points at the shared trial reference point
pB <- ggplot(emmSharedPt, aes(x = nat_or_art, y = prob)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(color = nat_or_art), size = 2, alpha = 0.7,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = canopyCols,
                     labels = c(artificial = "Artificial", naturalistic = "Naturalistic")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0.25, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Stimulus type", y = "Predicted P(correct) at trial 26", color = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

```{r supplementaryTbls}
roundNumsInString <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  vapply(
    x,
    function(s) {
      nums <- regmatches(s, gregexpr("-?[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*", s, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
      if (length(nums) == 0) return(s)
      out     <- s
      rounded <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), as.numeric(nums))
      for (i in seq_along(nums)) out <- sub(nums[i], rounded[i], out, fixed = TRUE)
      out
    },
    character(1)
  )
}
```

```{r tbl-s-overview}
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted $P_{\\mathrm{corr}}$ at key trial positions and test--control contrasts for all experiments. Control start and contrast columns are blank for test-only experiments."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"

  left_join(
    contrastRes$contrastsTbl %>% select(experiment, logOddsRatio95CI, pFmt),
    by = "experiment"
  ) %>%
  left_join(nSummary, by = "experiment") %>%
  mutate(experiment = factor(experiment, levels = expOrder)) %>%

  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(as.character(experiment), !!!c(artLabels, natcanLabels)))

n_nat    <- sum(allExpOverview$nat_or_art == "naturalistic")

tbl <- allExpOverview %>%
  select(experiment, firstPcorr95CI, midPcorr95CI, lastTestPcorr95CI,
         ctrlStartPcorr95CI, logOddsRatio95CI, pFmt) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Experiment", "Test start", "Test middle", "Test end",
                  "Control start", "Log-odds ratio [95% CI]", "P"),
    booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(" " = 1, "$P_{\\\\mathrm{corr}}$ [95\\\\% CI]" = 4, " " = 2),
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Artificial", 1, n_art) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Naturalistic", n_art + 1, n_art + n_nat) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9, latex_options = "hold_position")

# knitr::kable converts non-ASCII chars to <U+XXXX> sequences; fix them here
# after all kableExtra processing (which would re-escape LaTeX backslashes)
knitr::asis_output(
  gsub("<U\\+00B0>", "$^{\\\\circ}$",
  gsub("<U\\+00B1>", "$\\\\pm$",
  gsub("<U\\+2014>", "---",
  gsub("< ", "$<$ ",
       paste(as.character(tbl), collapse = "\n")))))
)
```

```{r tbl-s-sample-sizes}
#| tbl-cap: "Per-experiment sample sizes and test-phase duration. Wasps and choices are split by phase (test and control). Last trial is the highest trial number reached in the test phase. Control columns are blank for test-only experiments."
```

```{r supp-model-table-prep}
#| include: false
suppArtModelData <- mAllCoefsTbl %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "artificial") %>%
  mutate(experiment = forcats::fct_relevel(experiment, q2ArtTableOrder)) %>%
  arrange(experiment, term)

suppNatModelData <- mAllCoefsTbl %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic") %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(natcanLabels))
  ) %>%
  arrange(experiment, term)

suppModelData <- bind_rows(suppArtModelData, suppNatModelData)

# Group anchors for pack_rows — art block
suppArtModelGroups <- suppArtModelData %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    end   = cumsum(n),
    start = end - n + 1,
    label = unname(artLabels[as.character(experiment)])
  )

# Group anchors for pack_rows — nat block (row indices continue after art block)
artNRows <- nrow(suppArtModelData)
suppNatModelGroups <- suppNatModelData %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    end   = artNRows + cumsum(n),
    start = end - n + 1,
    label = as.character(experiment)
  )

suppModelTable <- suppModelData %>%
  select(term, logOdds95CI, pFmt)
```

```{r tbl-s-model-coefs}
#| tbl-cap: "Model coefficients for all experiments. Fixed effects: trial number, side alternation, reward side, and (for experiments with a control phase) experiment phase (manipulation) and its interaction with trial number. Random effect: individual ID."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"
k <- knitr::kable(
  suppModelTable,
  col.names = c("Term", "Log-odds [95% CI]", "P"),
  booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE
)
allGroups <- bind_rows(suppArtModelGroups, suppNatModelGroups)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(allGroups))) {
  k <- kableExtra::pack_rows(k,
    allGroups$label[i],
    allGroups$start[i],
    allGroups$end[i]
  )
}
knitr::asis_output(
  gsub("<U\\+2014>", "---",
  gsub("< ", "$<$ ",
       paste(as.character(k), collapse = "\n")))
)
```

## Additional experiments

```{r fig-supp-experiments}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Wasp performance for two additional \"control\" experiments not included in the main analysis. A) In this experiment we first tested whether a group of wasps could discriminate a naturalistic pair of stimuli (left panel, same data as presented in @fig-q3-tc). To rule out that performance differences between naturalistic and artificial stimuli might be driven by differences in wasp species, hives, individuals or phase of the season, we tested if the same group of wasps could discriminate the perpendicular-parallel artificial stimuli immediately following the naturalistic canopy (right panel, post-natcan). Note that the same wasp individuals that can not discriminate among naturalistic stimuli can discriminate artificial stimuli. B) In this experiment we ruled out the possibility that above-chance discrimination of dorsal stimuli might be explained by the wasps using reflections of the dorsal stimuli off surfaces of the Y-maze that are not dorsal to the wasps (eg. the bottom or ventral part of the maze). To preclude the use of reflections we covered different parts of the inside of the first chamber with diffuser paper that reduces specular reflections. We first covered the bottom of the first chamber (middle panel) and subsequently the side-walls as well (right-most panel). Note that performance remains well above chance after the addition of diffuser paper."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"
print(suppFig)
```

## Canopy G1

```{r fig-supp-canopyG1}
#| fig-cap: "Wasp reward navigation performance for the Canopy G1 naturalistic stimulus experiment. Format is the same as in @fig-q3-tc."
#| fig-height: 2

g1ID <- "natcan3_080825"

emmG1All <- emmAll %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
emmG1Pts <- emmPts %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID, trial_pos %in% c("last_test", "ctrl_start")) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
rollG1 <- choices_rolling %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))

pG1 <- ggplot(emmG1All, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = rollG1, aes(x = rank_trial, y = pcorr), colour = "black", alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_errorbar(data = emmG1Pts, aes(x = rank_trial, ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), width = 2) +
  geom_point(data = emmG1Pts, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_text(
    data = nLabels %>%
      filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
      mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels),
             manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))),
    aes(label = label),
    x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_grid(experiment ~ manipulation, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(experiment = as_labeller(natcanImgLabels))) +
  ylab("% correct") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.text.y.right = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0),
        strip.background = element_blank())

pG1
```
